country: # Catalunya: kiting is banned on all Catalan beaches 1 Jun–30 Sep except in authorised kite zones.

name: Sant Pere Pescador
notes: Kite areas of about 200 m each: Cortal de la Vila (schools and free riding) and Cortal de la Devesa (run by the La Ballena Alegre campsite); authorised summer kite zone, stay in the marked channels. Tramuntana and summer thermal. Also: Empuriabrava – La Rubina (5 km north, easterlies).

name: Castelldefels
notes: Town kite zone 1 Jun–mid Sep at Platja de la Pineda, between Carrer 9 and Carrer 11: weekdays 15–19 h only (2026), closed weekends and holidays, free licence and vest from the office at Passeig Marítim 159. Outside those hours kiting is banned in summer. Free the rest of the year.

name: Riumar (Ebro delta)
notes: Mainly an autumn–spring spot: best in mestral (NW, cross-shore); summer southerlies are offshore. Schools ride a signposted zone; one guide says the beach is closed to kites in summer. Check the signs on site.

name: Platja dels Eucaliptus (Ebro delta)
notes: Shallow water at the root of the Trabucador, where the schools teach; beginner-friendly. In summer ride only the signposted kite zone.

name: El Trabucador (Ebro delta)
notes: Summer thermal (S) spot; flat, shallow water on the Badia dels Alfacs (west) side, about 1 m deep in places. Schools report signposted kite zones in summer.

country: # Comunitat Valenciana: summer kiting only in the few buoyed channels / zones.

name: Valencia – El Perellonet
notes: Municipal buoyed kite zone south of the Perellonet river mouth with Kitezone club (municipal lifeguard 14:30–19:30 in summer, 2017–18 tenders). Rules changed more than once: the Albufera park refused the canals in 2023, so check the club for the current season. Also: Sueca – Mareny de Barraquetes (summer channel for club members, free off-season).

name: Oliva
notes: Oliva Nova; in summer kiting only in the authorised zone (club rescue boat). Also: Dénia – Les Deveses (marked kite zone just south).

name: Santa Pola – Tamarit
notes: Town kite channel 120 m wide (council decree 9 Jul 2024, renewed yearly): Oct–May free; June and September free on weekdays, weekends 14–17 h only; Holy Week, July and August weekdays 14–17 h only, weekends banned. La Gola (south) is not open to kites. Also: Elche – Arenales del Sol (north).

name: Mar Menor – Los Narejos
notes: Flat-water lagoon, kite zone and school; E and SW (lebeche) most common. Also: Los Nietos (south shore, onshore in NE/E), La Manga – Isla del Ciervo.

name: Almerimar
notes: Poniente (W) spot by the marina: flat between the breakwaters, waves further out. Also: Roquetas de Mar – Las Salinas (levante).

name: Málaga – Los Álamos
notes: Málaga's kite zone (Guadalmar–Los Álamos), with schools. Afternoon poniente plus SW sea breeze, 15–20 kn in spring and summer; gusty and offshore towards evening. Crowded (up to 40 kites). Aena (airport) restricted kiting here in 2015 after a plane accident; check the current zone with a school.

country: # Andalucía — Strait and Cádiz Atlantic coast

name: Tarifa – Los Lances
notes: Los Lances Norte (Río Jara), the main Tarifa kite beach, all levels, levante or poniente. In summer there are marked zones for bathers, schools and free-riders: stay in them. The south of the beach is for bathing only. Exact summer dates not confirmed by an official source. Also: Tarifa – Balneario (experts only, strong levante).

name: Tarifa – Valdevaqueros
notes: Includes Punta Paloma. Levante is side-offshore (drift), poniente is the easy wind. Narrow summer riding area shared with bathers and windsurfers, very crowded; rocks in parts of the area. Not for beginners in strong levante.

name: Los Caños de Meca
locate: q:Playa de Los Caños de Meca
notes: Levante (E) spot, works from about force 6 in Tarifa; the wind is lighter than in the Strait. Reef and rocks on the beach; kiters launch down the point towards the Trafalgar lighthouse. Intermediate and above. A school page says part of the beach is reserved in summer and marked bathing zones must be respected; no official text found, ask a local school.

name: El Palmar (Vejer)
locate: q:Playa de El Palmar Vejer de la Frontera
notes: Poniente (W to NW) is the main wind; levante is weak here. Powerful shorebreak at high tide and a strong current in poniente: experienced riders. Mostly a surf beach. A spot guide says kiting is banned here in summer; no official text found, so treat summer as closed.

name: Chiclana – Sancti Petri
notes: La Barrosa beach, south end at Sancti Petri. Poniente (W to NW) works once strong; levante from the SSE also. The Sancti Petri island shelters it from west swell. Kite Surf Chiclana has run lessons on the beach since 2006. A spot guide says kiting is banned June to September; no official text found, ask the school.

name: El Portil
notes: Beach at the mouth of the Río Piedras, facing the El Rompido sandspit: schools (Flecha Extreme, Nómadas del Kite) teach here in shallow, sheltered water; strong currents at the river mouth. Also: Punta Umbría (open beach, waves).

name: Doniños (Ferrol)
notes: Exposed Atlantic beach with waves; kite area is the left side of the bay (Punta Penencia). Best in N–NE cross-shore wind, S–SW gets rough fast; experienced riders. Local crowd is protective: ride respectfully. Alternative: San Xurxo.

name: Razo (Carballo)
notes: Open Atlantic beach with waves and strong currents, best in NE wind; winter SW is hard to control. Experienced riders. Inside the Razo–Baldaio nature reserve: the lagoon behind is flat at high tide but stay out of it as the tide drops (bird sanctuary, kite ban feared).

name: A Lanzada
notes: Huge exposed beach with clean waves; best in SW–W wind from autumn to spring. Intermediate and up; rocks in the water and to the south. A spot guide says kiting is not allowed here in summer (no official text found): check with the schools. Also: O Grove – A Mexilloeira (sheltered ría, flat in N–NE).

name: Redondela – Cesantes
notes: Flat shallow water at the head of the Vigo ría (San Simón inlet); SW summer thermal in the afternoon, gusty NE off the land in high pressure. Home of the TMKiteClub and the Kitefest. Boats on the south side, sharp mussels in the sand. Also: Vigo – O Vao (flat behind Toralla island in W–NW).

name: Salinas – San Juan de Nieva
notes: Main west-wind spot of Asturias (SW to NW): a wide 3 km beach with strong wind and waves, for experienced riders. In bathing season kiters use a separate entrance and follow the lifeguards. Also: Gijón – El Arbeyal (NE and NW) and San Lorenzo (NE–E).

name: Somo
notes: Waves on the open beach; flat water in La Poza (Miera estuary), where the Northwind school teaches. NW and W work at any tide; NE and E are offshore and best at low to mid tide. SW is gusty (Los Peligros is the alternative). Never ride in the red and green buoyed channel to Pedreña. Guides mention a kite launch zone 15 Jun–15 Sep about 1 km west of the car park.

name: Embalse de La Loteta
notes: Reservoir ridden in the cierzo (NW), which blows along its length; south launch area with Club Kitesurf La Loteta. Shallow and rocky in places: check the water level.

name: Mallorca – Pollença (Sa Marina)
notes: Authorised kite zone and schools in the Bay of Pollença.

name: Mallorca – Son Serra de Marina
locate: q:Platja de Son Serra de Marina
notes: Island's main kite beach Oct–May; summer restrictions. Also: Platja de Muro (small authorised channel).

name: Menorca – Cala Tirant
notes: Waves with the tramuntana (N); summer: designated launch area only.

name: Fuerteventura – Sotavento
notes: Tidal lagoon: flat and shallow for a few hours around high tide, mostly on spring tides; at low tide a long walk to the water. Check the tide table. Cross-offshore trade wind, gusty in summer. Beginner friendly, World Cup venue.

name: Lanzarote – Famara
notes: Waves, trade wind; currents.

name: Lanzarote – Costa Teguise
notes: Las Cucharas bay: calmer inside, chop and swell outside; schools. Gusty close to shore when the wind is too northerly. Los Charcos, 500 m upwind, is the expert-only shallow wave spot.

name: Gran Canaria – Pozo Izquierdo
notes: Very strong trade wind, lava-rock entry (worse at low tide), waves with swell: experts only. Riders launch from the Salinas side, south of the bay; the bay beach itself is reported closed to kiters (no official text found), so ask locally.

name: Tenerife – El Médano
notes: Trade wind May–Oct; shallow water at the north end.

name: Liencres (Valdearenas)
notes: E wind is the stable one (side-shore, best at low to mid tide); NE, W and NW also work. Waves and currents: not for beginners. Parking is difficult in summer.

name: Oriñón
notes: Beach near Castro-Urdiales listed by spot guides for kiting, with few details on wind. Check conditions on site.

name: Ereaga (Getxo)
notes: Bilbao estuary beach: NW and SW winds work best, pure W is gusty. Freeride conditions unless there is a big swell. Water quality is poor (port and industry).

name: La Arena (Muskiz)
notes: Onshore NW wind in winter; freeride works without swell, moderate waves at low tide. Strong shorebreak at high tide; not for beginners.

name: Gorliz
notes: Sheltered bay with cleaner water than the Bilbao beaches; slightly gusty WNW wind, a wave breaks by the mole in swell. Onshore wind and the road behind: experienced riders.

name: Laida (Mundaka)
notes: Urdaibai estuary mouth with strong tidal currents; best in S to SW wind, flat water in the river at high tide. Experts only.

name: Zarautz
notes: Mainly a surf beach: kiting needs a strong WNW wind, the beach narrows at high tide and the left side is gusty when the wind goes more westerly. Crowded in summer.

name: Zurriola (Donostia)
notes: Strong W wind for waves, NW onshore for kiting only. Bathers and surfers share the beach (marked surf zones in summer) and shorebreak is strong at high tide; no kite article found in the beach rules, so ask the lifeguards.

name: Gran Canaria – Arinaga
notes: Flat to choppy water, steady trade wind, long pebbly beach; intermediate riders. Best May–September.

name: Pals

name: Segur de Calafell

name: Cambrils (Platja del Regueral)

name: L'Hospitalet de l'Infant
notes: Long beach south of the village; garbí and levante. The council has opened a marked kite zone on Platja de l'Arenal (before Camping Cala d'Oques); if it runs this summer, kiting is allowed there.

name: L'Almadrava (Vandellòs)
notes: Quiet beach south of L'Hospitalet; garbí and levante.

name: L'Ampolla (Platja de l'Arenal)
notes: Shallow beach facing the Badia del Fangar; good for learning.

name: Punta del Fangar (Ebro delta)
notes: Remote sandspit at the north of the delta; access on foot; flat water in the bay. No school or marked kite zone here: ride only if you know the spot.

name: Badalona
notes: City beach north of Barcelona; levante and gregal days.

name: Montgat
notes: Small beach north of Badalona; levante.

name: Vilassar de Mar

name: Vilanova i la Geltrú (La Farola)
notes: Town beach by the lighthouse; garbí and levante.

name: Creixell
notes: Beach west of Torredembarra; garbí and levante.

name: Altafulla
notes: Beach east of Tarragona; garbí and levante.

name: Barcelona – Barceloneta
notes: City beach; the city bans kiting 1 Jun–30 Sep. Off-season levante / gregal days only, away from the boat channels.

name: Sant Martí d'Empúries
notes: Beach in the Gulf of Roses south of Sant Pere Pescador; easterlies; tramuntana side-off.

name: L'Escala (Platja dels Riells)
notes: Town beach at the south end of the Gulf of Roses; tramuntana and easterlies. Packed with swimmers in summer.

name: Platja d'Aro
notes: Town beach; garbí (SW summer thermal) cross-shore. Gregal and levante bring shorebreak and chop, not for beginners. Quieter by the Ridaura mouth; the wind drops south of the harbour wall.

name: Mallorca – Es Barcarès (Alcúdia)
notes: Bay of Pollença side of Alcúdia; northerlies; summer restrictions.

name: Mallorca – Platja d'Alcúdia

notes: Bay of Palma, south and south-west winds; best in winter. Crowded with bathers in summer, light thermal only; summer restrictions apply. Experienced riders.

name: Mallorca – S'Arenal (Playa de Palma)
notes: Bay of Palma, east end of Playa de Palma; best outside the main season, kitable much of the year. Club Náutico S'Arenal; summer restrictions apply.

name: Mallorca – Santa Ponça
notes: Bay on the south-west coast; a winter spot, in summer almost no room on the water. Summer restrictions apply.

name: Mallorca – Sa Ràpita
notes: Long sandy beach of Es Trenc on the south coast; shallow flat water, thermal and frontal winds; kite school on site (Cuatro Vientos). Summer restrictions apply.

name: Menorca – Punta Prima
notes: South-east corner of Menorca; a good spot in north-easterly winds after a tramuntana or mistral. Kite station on the beach; practicable only in the low season (Nov–May).

name: Ibiza – Platja d'en Bossa
notes: South coast of Ibiza, NE, E and SE winds. Kiting is only allowed in the low season (Nov–May); unavailable in summer. Chop and small waves. Built-up beach, check the signs.

name: Ibiza – Cala Martina

name: Formentera – Ses Illetes
notes: Park beach at Ses Salines with flat turquoise water; a known Balearic spot outside the tourist season. Kiting banned May–Oct inside the Ses Salines park per tourist-board sources. Rentals and courses on the beach.

name: Formentera – Platja de Migjorn (Ca Marí)
notes: Long south-coast beach; works in light easterlies for freeride, shorebreak when the wind is strong. Summer restrictions apply near bathers.

name: Algeciras – Getares
notes: Levante spot, a calmer fallback when Tarifa is above about 30 knots; onshore wind, intermediate and advanced riders. A travel site reports no kiting 15 Jun–15 Sep; official source not found, so not encoded.

name: Valdoviño – A Frouxeira
notes: Long sandy beach with big, disorganised waves that break close in at high tide and a strong rip: experts only, a jumping spot rather than a long-ride one. Works in the usual high-pressure NE and in low-pressure westerlies. Crowded with sunbathers in summer. Easier option nearby: San Xurxo.

name: Ares (Ría de Ares)
notes: Sheltered sickle-shaped bay on the Ría de Ares: works fairly regularly in low-pressure cross-onshore SW wind, with chop in open water. Rocks on the sand and in the water, shorebreak in bigger swell, power cables along the road behind the beach. Flat lagoon at Razo–Baldaio is the winter flat-water option.

name: Santa Cristina (Oleiros)
notes: A Coruña's city kite spot, 1.5 km beach in the Canaval cove with calm, deep water; popular with freeriders and beginners. Kite school on site (Kiteskull). No official kite rule found.

name: Fornos (Ortigueira)
notes: Launch from Playa de Morouzos in the Ría de Santa María estuary. Gusty S wind for freeride; strong NE brings waves but only around high tide. Strong currents at the river mouth.

name: Laxe
notes: Very sheltered bay: water stays flat behind the harbour walls even in strong NE wind. Hardly anyone kites here.

name: Carnota
notes: Long beach on the Costa da Morte: sunny summer days strengthen N–NE wind, giving easy chop sessions or a clean beach break depending on swell. Kite schools from Santiago run lessons here.

name: Ancoradoiro (Monte Louro)
notes: Beach and lagoon at the foot of Monte Louro: summer thermal wind, clean mid-size waves. Shorebreak at high tide; winter SW swell is too big.

name: Corrubedo – A Ladeira
notes: Dune beach where N–NW wind is thermally strengthened to force 5–7 from June to September (local funnel between dunes and headland). Usually flat, clean waves with swell. Very gusty in onshore S–SW; surf too big. The dunes and river mouth are a nature reserve: landing there can bring a fine of several hundred euros.

name: Aguieira (Ría de Muros)
notes: Wide, sheltered sandy beach with flat water; cross-onshore N–NE wind from spring to summer, often dropping around noon and picking up in the evening. Popular kite scene, more kiters than windsurfers.

name: Agrelo (Sanxenxo)
notes: Beach for all levels; kite guides give N, NW and NNW as the wind. Parking, showers and toilets. No official kite rule found.

country: # pro: Windy markers the 2 km rule had left out (WHE-129)

name: Tarifa – Punta Paloma
notes: Dune beach just north of Valdevaqueros, a different entrance (pine forest and military-base side), about 3 km from the Valdevaqueros pin. Levante and poniente both work; shelter at the foot of the dune in westerlies. Crowded in high season, quieter off season. Guides disagree on level (any level vs experienced): treat as intermediate and above. Summer kite zone rules as for Valdevaqueros: ask a school.

name: Torremolinos – Playamar
notes: Torremolinos beach south of Los Álamos, same summer poniente thermal. A spot guide calls it mainly for a first try or an occasional session; Torremolinos schools run courses on these beaches. Check the Málaga and Torremolinos beach rules in summer.
